problems.title: URL shortener
problems.ask: Design a URL shortener like bit.ly. Support 100M new URLs/day, 10B redirects/day, with sub-100ms p99 redirect latency. URLs never expire.
deep_dive_targets: ID generation strategy (base62 counter vs hash vs Snowflake)
cache topology (CDN edge + Redis L2)
follow_ups: Custom aliases — how do you prevent collision while keeping the counter approach?
Analytics on clicks — how do you not block the redirect path?
Abuse detection — phishing URLs at scale?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Picking MD5/SHA hash of the URL as the short ID. Hash collisions force you into retry-on-collision logic that breaks idempotency. A monotonic counter encoded base62 is the boring-correct answer.

problems.title: Twitter home timeline
problems.ask: Design Twitter's home timeline. A user logs in and sees a feed of tweets from people they follow, ranked by recency. 500M users, average 200 follows, 1B tweets/day, p99 timeline load under 200ms.

sources.ref: Twitter — Manhattan, the real-time storage stack

uses_for: hybrid fan-out (push for normal, pull for celebrities)

deep_dive_targets: Fan-out on write vs fan-out on read (and the hybrid)
Timeline cache structure (per-user materialized list)
follow_ups: How do you handle a user with 100M followers (Obama)?
How do you mix in promoted tweets without blocking the read path?
How do you backfill timelines when a user follows someone new?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Picking pure fan-out on write and not addressing the celebrity case. At 100M followers, a single tweet would write 100M timeline entries — fan-out collapses. The answer is hybrid: fan-out for normal users, pull on read for celebrities.

problems.title: WhatsApp messaging
problems.ask: Design WhatsApp. 2B users, 100B messages/day, p99 delivery latency under 1s. Support 1-to-1 and group chats up to 1024 members. Online/offline presence, read receipts, and end-to-end encryption.

sources.ref: Discord — how we store billions of messages

deep_dive_targets: Message ordering across multiple senders to the same recipient
Connection management at 2B concurrent persistent connections
follow_ups: How do you guarantee in-order delivery when client reconnects after going offline?
How does end-to-end encryption interact with group chat membership changes?
How do you handle a group chat with 1024 active members typing simultaneously?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Picking HTTP polling for delivery. At 2B users polling every few seconds, you'd serve 100B+ requests/min for empty replies. WebSocket or XMPP-style persistent connections are mandatory; the architecture must support millions of idle connections per server.

problems.title: Distributed cache (Redis/Memcached-class)
problems.ask: Design a distributed in-memory cache, like Memcached or Redis-cluster. 10TB total working set, 1M ops/sec, p99 under 1ms. Tolerate node failures without losing cache coherence.
deep_dive_targets: Consistent hashing with virtual nodes (vnode count, ring rebalance)
Thundering herd / cache stampede mitigation (lease tokens, request coalescing)
follow_ups: What happens when one key gets 100k QPS (hot key)?
How do you do cross-region replication without doubling write cost?
What's your eviction policy and why?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Using modulo-N hashing for shard assignment. When a node is added, ~100% of keys remap — cache cold-start. Consistent hashing with virtual nodes is the answer; expect the interviewer to draw the ring.

problems.title: Rate limiter
problems.ask: Design a distributed rate limiter. 10M users, each with their own quotas (e.g. 100 req/min). Decisions must be made in under 5ms p99. Quotas must hold even under burst traffic across multiple API servers.

sources.ref: Cloudflare — how we built rate limiting capable of scaling to millions of domains
Stripe — scaling your API with rate limiters

deep_dive_targets: Token bucket vs fixed window vs sliding window log vs sliding window counter
Edge enforcement vs centralized counters (Redis cluster)
follow_ups: What if Redis is temporarily unavailable?
How do you handle a user with 100 requests landing on 50 different API servers simultaneously?
Can you do it without any centralized state?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Picking fixed-window counters and missing the burst-at-window-boundary issue. A user can do 2x quota by sending bursts right before and after the window resets. Sliding-window-counter (or token bucket) is the boring-correct default.

problems.title: Stripe-style payment processing
problems.ask: Design Stripe's core payment processing. Process 100M payments/day, each transaction must be exactly-once (no double-charges), reconcile with a downstream double-entry ledger, and survive partial bank failures.

sources.ref: Stripe — designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency

deep_dive_targets: Idempotency key lifecycle and storage
Double-entry ledger with eventual reconciliation
follow_ups: What happens if Stripe's call to the bank times out — is the payment captured or not?
How do you reconcile a bank's nightly settlement file against your ledger?
How do webhooks guarantee at-least-once delivery without flooding the merchant?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Treating it as 'just a transaction.' The hardest part is *unknown* outcomes — the bank API timed out, did the payment go through? Idempotency keys + reconciliation jobs are the answer; 2PC across Stripe and a bank doesn't exist.

problems.title: Kafka (distributed log)
problems.ask: Design Kafka. Append-only partitioned log, 1M writes/sec per topic, durable replication, consumers can replay from any offset. Support exactly-once delivery semantics for downstream stream processors.
deep_dive_targets: ISR (in-sync replica) protocol and unclean leader election trade-off
Exactly-once via transactional producer (TID + commit marker)
follow_ups: What happens during a leader election — can you lose committed messages?
How does the consumer group know where to resume after rebalance?
Why is partition reassignment slow and what would you optimize?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Conflating 'at-least-once' with 'exactly-once.' Kafka EOS requires the transactional producer + idempotent send + consumer reading committed only. Many candidates wave hands; the depth signal is naming the marker offsets.

problems.title: DynamoDB-style KV store
problems.ask: Design a Dynamo-style distributed key-value store. Always-writable, even during network partition. 100k writes/sec, 1KB values, 99.99% availability single-region.

uses_for: JVM GC issues with hint queues

deep_dive_targets: Sloppy quorum + hinted handoff (the AP mechanism)
Vector clocks + sibling reconciliation
follow_ups: What if the hint queue grows unbounded during a long partition?
How do you handle concurrent writes during partition?
Why not Paxos here — wouldn't that give linearizability?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Picking strict quorum and missing that the prompt says 'always-writable.' CAP forces a choice; this prompt mandates AP. Strict quorum is CP. Citing 'eventually consistent' is empty without explaining the *mechanism* — hinted handoff + Merkle anti-entropy.

problems.title: Ad-click aggregator
problems.ask: Design a system that aggregates ad clicks for billing. 10B clicks/day, advertisers see dashboards updated within 1 minute, billing is correct to the cent (no double-counting, no missing clicks).
deep_dive_targets: Watermarks and late-arriving events
Exactly-once aggregation across re-processing
follow_ups: An ad server fails over and re-emits the last 30s of clicks — how do you avoid double-counting?
How do you handle 1% of clicks arriving 6 hours late from a flaky region?
How do you detect fraudulent click farms without slowing the path?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Treating it as a batch problem ('process every hour'). Advertisers need near-real-time dashboards AND billing accuracy. Lambda architecture (speed + batch) is the historical answer; kappa (stream-only with reprocessing) is the modern answer — name both.

problems.title: Distributed counter / leaderboard
problems.ask: Design a real-time leaderboard for a multiplayer game. 100M players, 1M score updates/sec at peak, leaderboard query returns top-100 globally in under 50ms. Approximate counts are acceptable; exact is preferred.

sources.ref: Redis — using sorted sets for leaderboards

deep_dive_targets: Sharded counter with merge (G-counter CRDT)
Top-K query under partitioned sorted sets
follow_ups: What if a single player's score is updated 10k times per second (hot key)?
How do you support 'rank around me' (player N's neighbors)?
How does it work across 5 geo regions?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Putting all scores in a single Redis sorted set. At 1M updates/sec, single-instance Redis is a bottleneck. Sharded sorted sets + periodic merge is the answer; for true top-K, a tournament tree of shard tops.

problems.title: LLM inference serving
problems.ask: Design a system that serves LLM completions at 10k QPS across a fleet of GPUs, with p95 latency under 2s. Average prompt is 4k tokens; average output is 500 tokens. Support both streaming and unary responses.

sources.ref: Anthropic — engineering challenges of serving Claude

deep_dive_targets: KV cache lifecycle on GPU memory (allocation, eviction, sharing across requests)
Continuous batching loop and scheduler
follow_ups: What if a single prompt is 100k tokens (long-context routing)?
How do you A/B test a new model version live?
What's the cache key for prompt cache — full prompt? prefix? both?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Treating it as a stateless web service. KV cache changes everything — each in-flight request holds GPU memory proportional to context length. Continuous batching is the headline optimization; without it, GPU utilization sits at 20-30%.

problems.title: RAG over 1B documents
problems.ask: Design a retrieval-augmented generation system over 1B documents. Queries arrive at 1k QPS, p99 retrieval latency under 200ms. The corpus is updated continuously (~100k new docs/hour). Support hybrid search (vector + keyword).
deep_dive_targets: HNSW graph + incremental updates (the freshness problem)
Hybrid search ranking (BM25 + vector score fusion)
follow_ups: How do you support a 100k new docs/hour update rate while keeping search latency stable?
Why not just use Elasticsearch with vector support?
How do you choose chunk size, and what's the trade-off?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Picking exact-kNN search and missing that 1B vectors at exact-kNN means a full scan per query. Approximate kNN via HNSW (or IVF, ScaNN) is mandatory. The interview signal is naming the recall/latency trade-off explicitly.

problems.title: Time-series DB at Datadog scale
problems.ask: Design a time-series DB that ingests 10M data points/sec, supports queries like 'avg CPU over last 1h for service=api, region=us-east, percentile=95'. Retention 13 months. Query p99 under 500ms.

sources.ref: Datadog — Husky, a TSDB for event observability

deep_dive_targets: Ingestion pipeline: from agent to durable storage (Kafka → consumer → Parquet)
Cardinality explosion mitigation (label store, query planning)
follow_ups: What happens when one customer suddenly emits 1M unique label combinations?
How do you support sub-second freshness while writing Parquet to S3?
How do you downsample without losing percentile accuracy?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Treating it as 'just a NoSQL DB.' TSDBs are dominated by the *cardinality* problem (number of unique label combinations). Solving 'metric name + labels' as a regular index causes O(cardinality) explosion; the answer is a separate cardinality-bounded label store + per-series chunks.

problems.title: Distributed tracing
problems.ask: Design a distributed tracing system like Datadog APM or Honeycomb. 1M spans/sec ingested, p99 query latency under 1s for 'show me all traces matching service=foo AND error=true in the last 1h'. 7 day retention.
deep_dive_targets: Head vs tail sampling (when each is right, where each costs you)
Trace assembly: stitching spans across services without a central coordinator
follow_ups: How do you decide to keep a trace if the decision must be made at the first hop (head sampling)?
How do you avoid each service phoning home to ask 'should I sample this trace'?
How does the service map get built — joining millions of spans?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Confusing trace context propagation (the protocol — W3C trace-context header) with sampling (the policy — what to keep). They're orthogonal; you must address both. Also: tail sampling requires holding ALL spans of a trace in memory before deciding, which is non-trivial at 1M spans/sec.

problems.title: Spanner-style globally-distributed SQL
problems.ask: Design a globally-distributed SQL database with external consistency — reads see a snapshot of the entire database at a globally-consistent point in time. Multi-region writes, p99 commit latency under 100ms intra-region, under 500ms cross-region.

uses_for: HLC (hybrid logical clock) alternative to TrueTime

deep_dive_targets: TrueTime API and how it bounds clock uncertainty (and what happens without it)
Two-phase commit on top of Paxos-replicated shards
follow_ups: What if you don't have GPS+atomic clocks (i.e., you're not Google)?
How do read-only transactions get global consistency without locks?
What's the failure case if TT.now()'s uncertainty bound grows large?
problems.trap_for_juniors: Treating TrueTime as 'fancy clocks.' The real insight is that TrueTime exposes *uncertainty* — `TT.now()` returns `[earliest, latest]` interval. Commit waits until that interval passes the commit timestamp. Without bounded uncertainty, you can't achieve external consistency without coordination on every read.
